clinician.trajectory_summary: A 14-year-old girl with established primary hypoparathyroidism diagnosed at age 9 (presenting with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and inappropriately low serum PTH) developed treatment-related complications. Following 5 years of calcium and 1-α-hydroxycholecalciferol therapy, she experienced a January 2015 episode of severe hypercalcemia requiring intensive fluid therapy, loop diuretics, and temporary withdrawal of supplements. By September 2015, she developed bilateral nephrocalcinosis (increased echogenicity of renal pyramids) with persistent hypercalciuria (urine Ca/Cr ratio 0.24 mg/mg) despite preserved renal function (eGFR 92 ml/min/1.73 m2). Admission revealed ongoing hypoparathyroidism (low PTH, hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia), oral candidiasis on swab culture, normal bone densitometry, and an incidental duplex left kidney with mild upper-pole collecting system dilatation (10 mm).
